Read out of saint.gr's line for 31 Μαρτίου, «Όσιος Ακάκιος ο Ομολογητής επίσκοπος Μελιτηνής», with the rank word and the see left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's second heading for the Julian 17 April, „Св. Акакије еп. Мелитински.“, with Св. left off — it is not a rank — and with еп. Мелитински left off, a rank this folder already carries in `types` and a see this corpus keeps in `office`. The heading gives no epithet beyond the see, so the bare forename is what is left. Measured, and the reader's prediction was wrong: `corpus-gate.mjs` run without `--batch` lists `? "акакије" — acacius-of-melitene, acacius-the-kausokalyvite`, and `acacius-the-kausokalyvite` already held this same bare Serbian form. A deliberate fold, recorded in the run's findings; the thirteen other folders of this spelling carry no Serbian form.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 17 aprilie — «Sfântul Ierarh Acachie, Episcopul Melitinei Armeniei»

feast.note: The Greek calendar keeps an Acacius the Confessor, bishop of Melitene, on 31 March, where the Romanian row on this folder holds 17 April. The same saint.gr page says that S. Eustratiades claims there was also an Acacius II, bishop of Melitene, and puts that one's feast on 18 April — so the site itself allows two bishops of this name and this see on two April days. The row records the day page that was read, and the identification with the man this folder already keeps rests on the see, the rank and the fifth-century anti-Nestorian work, which are the page's own; it is set down as a reading and not as a certainty, because a second folder for one man would be worse than an open question.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 31ης Μαρτίου — «Όσιος Ακάκιος ο Ομολογητής επίσκοπος Μελιτηνής»

attestations.note: The page heads him «(431 - ;)» and says «Ο Όσιος Ακάκιος έζησε τον πέμπτο αιώνα μ.Χ. (γεννήθηκε περί το 431 μ.Χ.)», born about 431 — and then has him distinguish himself when the heresy of Nestorius, patriarch of Constantinople, troubled the Church, write against Nestorius, and leave a surviving homily delivered at Ephesus. Those two statements cannot both stand: the Council of Ephesus met in 431. The year is the page's own and is recorded in `dates` with the contradiction named, and nothing is inferred to mend it. The page also credits him with virtue, learning and Orthodox zeal and calls him a most able speaker and teacher of the people. It prints no hymn; the one this folder carries is the Romanian troparion.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 30.04.2026 (17. април ст. ст.) — „Св. Акакије еп. Мелитински.“

attestations.note: The day's second entry, **on the Romanian calendar's day and not the Greek one**: doxologia keeps him on 17 April and saint.gr on 31 March; one row per church, so the Greek row kept its day and nothing moved. The entry is the fullest account of him read for this folder and almost all of it is new: that he struggled in the city he was born in, Melitene in Armenia; that **blessed Otrius, bishop of that city, who took part in the Second Ecumenical Council, ordained him presbyter**, and that he became bishop on Otrius's death; that he took part in the Third Ecumenical Council at Ephesus, which condemned Nestorius's blasphemy against the Mother of God, and **was zealous there for the purity of the Orthodox faith together with Cyril of Alexandria**; that he had great grace from God and worked many wonders; and that after a long and zealous service of God he **reposed peacefully in 435**. **That year is a contradiction and is recorded as one, not resolved**: this folder's only date is saint.gr's «γεννήθηκε περί το 431», a birth about 431, which the folder's own note already says cannot be reconciled with his preaching at Ephesus in that same year — and a death in 435 cannot stand beside a birth in 431 either. The Prologue's year is therefore recorded in `dates` as the death it is, and the note names the contradiction; no reader here chose between the two pages. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Îndreptător credinţei şi chip blândeţelor, învăţător înfrânârii te-a arătat pe tine, turmei tale, adevărul lucrurilor. Pentru aceasta ai dobândit cu smerenia cele înalte şi cu sărăcia cele bogate; Părinte Ierarhe Acachie, roagă pe Hristos Dumnezeu să mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfântului Ierarh Acachie, Episcopul Melitinei», Glasul 4

english.text: A rule of faith and a model of meekness, a teacher of abstinence — so has the truth of things shown you to your flock. Therefore you gained the heights by humility and riches by poverty. Father and hierarch Acacius, entreat Christ our God that our souls be saved.

birth.note: saint.gr: «Ο Όσιος Ακάκιος έζησε τον πέμπτο αιώνα μ.Χ. (γεννήθηκε περί το 431 μ.Χ.)» — the page's «περί», about, is why the display says about 431. The same page has him write against Nestorius and preach a surviving homily at Ephesus, where the council met in 431, which the year as printed cannot be reconciled with; the page's figure is recorded because it is the page's, and the contradiction is recorded with it rather than resolved. The Ohrid Prologue's death year, 435, cannot be reconciled with it either, and is recorded beside it for the same reason.

death.note: The Ohrid Prologue for 17. април ст. ст.: „После дуге и ревносне службе Богу сконча мирно, 435. год.“ — after a long and zealous service of God he reposed peacefully in 435. The folder held no death year before. **It contradicts the birth year recorded above**, saint.gr's about 431, which that page itself cannot reconcile with the council of 431 it has him preach at. Neither reading is chosen and neither is displaced: both stand as their pages print them, and each note names the other, which is how docs/CORPUS.md §3 asks a disagreement to be kept. doxologia, which keeps him on this day, gives no year either way.
